subject: Pilot extension: phased credit plan with SLA carve-out
messages:
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@holocorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@holocorp.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence & runway question

Thanks for the update earlier this morning. We wrapped the last internal demo and the engineering team wants another 4 weeks to stress test the inference at higher concurrency. Two procurement questions before we lock dates: 1) can you do a time-boxed extension (four weeks) without additional seat licenses? 2) if we need burst capacity beyond the included pilot hours, can Redwood provide phased credits that apply only to usage over the baseline rather than a straight term extension?

Also, we have a security review window scheduled Jan 10-14 — if there's any SLA carve-out language required for dedicated capacity during the test window, procurement needs that spelled out now.

— Sam
Senior ML Ops, HoloCorp

On Mon, Dec 20, 2026 at 09:05 Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hey Sam — great to hear the demo went well. We can certainly structure a 4-week timebox that leaves your seat licenses intact. Two quick notes: 1) we can offer phased usage credits that only kick in after your pilot baseline is consumed (example below), and 2) SLA carve-outs for dedicated routing are uncommon but we can document a conditional fallback and a limited SLA exception for scheduled stress tests.
>
> Proposed phased-credit example: baseline = 1M tokens for the pilot; overage buckets: next 500k tokens at 50% credit (applied as invoice credit), subsequent 500k at 25% credit. Total cost exposure is capped.
>
> If procurement is comfortable, I can draft a short amendment and share a redline-ready PDF. Looping procurement for visibility.
>
> Cheers,
> Priyom
> Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: procurement@holocorp.com
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Torres <sam.torres@holocorp.com>, Elena Varga <elena@holocorp.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Pilot cadence & runway question

Thanks — procurement here. A few clarifying points before we sign anything: 1) we need the credit mechanics and accounting flow (how credits appear on the invoice) and whether they expire; 2) we need a short clause that permits HoloCorp to request a one-time extension of the timebox by up to 2 weeks if the security window impacts testing; 3) confirm there are no hidden minimums or required prepayments for the burst buckets.

Please cc finance on the amendment when shared.

procurement@holocorp.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: procurement@holocorp.com, Sam Torres <sam.torres@holocorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot extension: phased credit plan with SLA carve-out

Thanks for the clear ask — summarized answers and next steps below. I copied Kimberly (legal/contract) and Marcus (billing) so we can get a redline and invoice example over to you tomorrow.

Summary answers:
- Credit mechanics: credits are issued as invoice line-item credits (negative line) applied to the month where overage occurred. Credits expire 90 days from issuance unless converted to a one-time invoice offset upon mutual agreement. We will show an example invoice PDF.
- Timebox extension: we can add a one-time safety extension clause: up to +14 days if the security window or other force majeure-like testing requirements overlap the original timebox. Extension is non-cumulative and must be requested at least 3 business days before the original end date.
- No hidden minimums: burst buckets are charged against usage and then credited per the phased schedule; no prepayment required for the initial 4-week extension.

Proposed amendment highlights (to be attached):
- 4-week extension to pilot run dates (no change to seat counts)
- Phased credits: first 500k overage tokens = 50% credit; next 500k = 25% credit; cap = 1M overage credits total
- SLA carve-out: scheduled stress-testing windows (documented in schedule A) receive a documented fallback policy; Redwood agrees not to apply penalty credits for planned capacity reconfiguration during that scheduled window.

Next steps: Kimberly will share a PDF amendment with tracked changes and Marcus will attach an invoice mock showing credits. If procurement signs off, we can publish a short DocuSign amendment and the pilot will resume on Jan 4, 2027.

Thanks —
Priyom
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: procurement@holocorp.com, Sam Torres <sam.torres@holocorp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot extension: phased credit plan with SLA carve-out

Hi Sam / procurement team — attaching the amendment PDF (Redwood_Pilot_Amendment_v1.pdf) and SOW update. Key legal points called out in the amendment: 1) credit expiry: 90 days; 2) extension clause: single 14-day extension, non-cumulative; 3) SLA carve-out language limited to scheduled stress-test windows and limited to routing/configuration changes only (does not waive core uptime commitments outside those windows).

Please review and reply with any requested redlines. If acceptable, we'll send via DocuSign next business day. Marcus attached an invoice sample in the PDF that shows how credits will appear as negative line items.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood_Pilot_Amendment_v1.pdf (amendment draft), SOW_HoloCorp_v3.docx (updated scope)
